question: By taking a suitable nearby value, use linear approximation to estimate $\frac{1}{\sqrt{15.8}}$.
explanation:
Selection of the function
Let $f(x)=x^{-\frac{1}{2}}$ and choose the nearby value $a=16$. Then
$$f(16)=\frac{1}{4}$$
Derivative at $x=16$
$$f'(x)=-\frac{1}{2x^{\frac{3}{2}}}$$
Since $16^{\frac{3}{2}}=64$,
$$f'(16)=-\frac{1}{128}$$
Change in $x$
$$15.8-16=-0.2$$
Linear approximation
$$f(15.8)\approx f(16)+f'(16)(-0.2)$$
$$f(15.8)\approx\frac{1}{4}+\frac{0.2}{128}$$
Simplification
$$f(15.8)\approx0.25+0.0015625=0.2515625$$
Conclusion
Hence, $\frac{1}{\sqrt{15.8}}\approx0.25156$.
